response:
It sounds like you're carrying a lot of guilt or worry about not being able to provide something for your daughter, even though she's an adult who managed on her own last year. That kind of pressure can weigh heavily on a parent, especially when finances are tight and you have four children to think about.

It might help to remember that your love and support aren't measured by what you can pay for. Your daughter is in her 20s and has already shown she can navigate things independently. Being honest with her about what's realistic right now is not a failure—it's part of a healthy adult relationship. If you'd like, it may help to talk openly with her about the situation together, so the responsibility doesn't feel like it rests only on you.

Is there a particular part of this that's troubling you most? I'm happy to listen.
